fields.name: pattern
fields.description: At the video cycle, identify the stationary marker grid and write the complete ordered list of demonstrated visited nodes, including the initial red node. Encode nodes as [row,column], using zero-based rows top to bottom and columns left to right in the front image. Follow the stick and changes in red endpoints and connecting traces chronologically. Do not add duplicates for repeated frames at one endpoint; do include genuine revisits and intermediate visited endpoints along collinear segments. During every act cycle copy the incoming list unchanged. e.g. [[2,1],[2,2],[1,2],[0,1]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of grid nodes visited in the demonstration, including the starting node and every subsequent segment endpoint. Represent each node as [row,column], with zero-based rows from top to bottom and columns from left to right in the front image. At the video cycle, extract the entire ordered path from stick motion, newly red endpoints, and connecting traces. Repeated frames of one visit add nothing; a genuine return to a node adds another occurrence. Preserve intermediate visited endpoints even when successive segments are collinear. Carry this list unchanged through execution. e.g. [[2,1],[2,2],[1,2],[0,1]]

fields.name: reached_index
fields.description: Write 0 during the video cycle and at execution step zero: the stick starts on pattern[0]. At later act cycles, inspect the current pose and the motion frames for arrival at pattern[incoming reached_index + 1]. If the stick has reached that node within 1 cm and the visible endpoint activation supports arrival, increment by one; otherwise retain the incoming value. Never increment merely because you are about to command a move. If no steps executed, retain the value. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Zero-based index in pattern of the latest consecutively reached demonstration endpoint during execution. Write 0 at the video cycle and at the initial execution cycle, where the stick already occupies the demonstrated starting node. At subsequent cycles, advance only when the observed execution has reached the next listed node, as established by the stick location and endpoint activation; accept positioning error within 1 cm. Record observed arrival, not the destination of the waypoint being chosen at this cycle. Otherwise retain the previous value. e.g. 1

action:
During the video cycle write memory only. Execution starts with the stick already at the first demonstrated node; do not command that starting pose again. Identify the square marker grid from the current front image, using the wrist image to resolve occlusion. Its spacing is 0.10 m and its center is (x,y)=(-0.10,0). For an N-by-N grid, node [r,c] has x=-0.10+0.10*(r-(N-1)/2) and y=0.10*(c-(N-1)/2). Thus upward in the front image means decreasing world x, and rightward means increasing world y. Count actual grid rows and columns, not just currently unobscured markers. Use calibration and visible markers to check this registration.

Determine the latest reached index using the incoming reached_index and observed arrival at its next node, applying the memory update rule. If another node remains, command exactly that next node's world x and y, z=0.070 m, retaining the current approximately downward TCP orientation. Keep the gripper closed (command -1; the stick interface ignores it). Move directly between successive demonstrated endpoints, including diagonals, without lifting, adding intermediate waypoints, or pausing to reproduce demonstration timing. Target the ideal grid coordinates rather than adding an offset to the imperfect current TCP pose. Arrival within 1 cm is sufficient to move on; do not unnecessarily correct the few-millimetre residual errors shown after motions.

If the next endpoint has not been reached, target that same endpoint rather than skipping it. If a motion executed no steps, do not advance progress; re-estimate the endpoint from the available images and retry a reachable, nonidentical waypoint toward it. If registration is uncertain, fit the regular 0.10 m grid to visible markers using calibration and the known current stick node, then use the best-supported next endpoint from pattern; do not invent a different pattern. Once the final endpoint is visibly reached, make no additional tracing motion; if another response is required before automatic termination, wait a single control step to allow success evaluation.
